Only local `path` dependencies are supported. Do not write `source`, `version`, or `commit`.

## E0904

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the dependency `{alias}` has no `path`
- `path`: write the directory of the package, such as `path "../textkit"`

Each dependency needs a `path` field.

## E0905

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: malformed language version `{version}`
- `form`: write three numbers separated by `.`, such as `0.0.3`

Language versions have three ASCII decimal numbers that fit in 64 bits, without leading zeroes except for zero itself.

## E0906

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: malformed hash `{hash}`
- `form`: write `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits

A dependency hash consists of `sha256:` and exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

## E0907

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: this file needs Benitoite {version} or later, but this is Benitoite {current}

The declared language version is newer than the interpreter. Use an interpreter at least as new as the declaration.

## E0908

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: this file was written for Benitoite {version}, and the language changed incompatibly in {changed}

The main message identifies the first incompatible language change after the declared version and no later than the interpreter's version. Notes list every applicable version and its summary in version order, and helps list the corresponding migration guidance in the same order, without source edits.

## E0909

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{item}` can be written only at the start of the starting file or in `package.bnt`

Imported modules cannot have `language` or `dependency` headers. A `package` block can be written only in `package.bnt`.

## E0910

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: a `package` block can be written only in `package.bnt`

Move the `package` block into `package.bnt` at the root.

## E0911

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: {what} is written both at the start of `{file}` and in `package.bnt`
- `other`: also written here

Write dependencies in one place, either the starting file or `package.bnt`. The same rule applies to `language` declarations.

## E0912

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `package.bnt` can contain only `language`, `dependency`, and `package`
- Label: not allowed in `package.bnt`

A settings file cannot contain imports or declarations.

## E0913

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{path}` is a settings file and cannot be checked, run, or tested

Do not specify `package.bnt` as a starting file. Check, run, or test the scripts that use it; `fmt` can format it.

## E0914

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the package `{package}` needs a `language` line

A `package.bnt` with a `package` block must declare the language version, even when checked as the root package.

## E0915

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: a package cannot have dependencies in this version
- `package`: this `package.bnt` declares the package `{package}`

A `package.bnt` with a `package` block cannot contain dependencies in this version.

## E0916

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: cannot read the dependency `{alias}` at `{path}`
- `reason`: {reason}

The dependency directory and its `package.bnt` must be readable.

## E0917

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the dependency `{alias}` at `{path}` is not a Benitoite package
- `no_config`: the directory has no `package.bnt`
- `no_block`: its `package.bnt` has no `package` block

A dependency must have `package.bnt` with a `package` block and a `language` line.

## E0918

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{module}` names both a module under the root directory and a module of the dependency `{alias}`
- `root_file`: under the root directory: `{root_path}`
- `package_file`: in the package `{package}`: `{package_path}`
- `rename`: rename the directory under the root directory, or the dependency

An import cannot refer to two different files. A root path and package path resolving to the same file are allowed.

## E0919

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the contents of the dependency `{alias}` do not match its `hash`
- `expected`: expected: {expected}
- `computed`: computed: {computed}
- `package`: package: `{package}`
- `update`: if the change is intended, write the computed hash

A dependency with `hash` must match the computed hash of its package contents. Update the declaration only if the change is intended.

## E0920

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: cannot compute the hash of the dependency `{alias}`
- `symlink`: `{path}` is a symbolic link
- `case`: `{path}` and `{other}` have the same path after conversion to Unicode lowercase
- `name`: `{path}` contains a newline
- `too_many`: the number of included files exceeds the limit of {limit}
- `too_many_entries`: the number of visited directory entries exceeds the limit of {limit}
- `too_large`: the total size of included files exceeds the limit of {limit} bytes
- `read`: cannot read `{path}`: {reason}
- `package`: package: `{package}`

The package hash rejects symbolic links, colliding lowercase paths, newline-containing paths, unreadable files, and packages exceeding the file count, directory entry count, or total size limit.

## E0921

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{path}` belongs to the dependency `{alias}` and cannot be imported as a root module
- Label: use the dependency alias
- `package`: package: `{package}`
- `import`: write `import {suggestion}`

A file under a declared dependency root must be imported through its dependency alias.

## E0922

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the dependency `{alias}` at `{path}` overlaps another root
- Label: invalid dependency root
- `root`: a dependency root cannot be the root directory itself or an ancestor of it
- `dependency`: dependency roots cannot be equal or contain one another
- `other`: the overlapping dependency `{other}` is declared here

Choose a dependency directory that does not contain the starting root and does not overlap another dependency root.

## E0923

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the dependency `{alias}` is already declared
- Label: existing dependency

Use a different alias or update the existing dependency.

## E0924

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the dependency `{alias}` is not declared

Specify an alias declared in the entry or package.bnt.

## E0925

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: there are no header items to move

The entry must contain language or dependency declarations.

## E0926

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{path}` already contains language or dependency declarations
- Label: existing declaration

Do not overwrite existing declarations when moving the entry header.

## E0927

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: cannot choose a file for the dependency declaration
- `entry`: specify an entry file, or create package.bnt

A root without an entry and without package.bnt has no destination.

## E0928

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: cannot move the header of `package.bnt`

Specify an entry file rather than the configuration file.

## E0929

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: malformed recorded effects

The effects field must be empty or a comma-separated list of uppercase names such as Console.Write, File.Read. It records the last package command report and is not checked against package contents during loading.

## E1001

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: cannot read the component `{path}`
- `reason`: {reason}

The component must be a readable file within the allowed directory.

## E1002

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: malformed component path `{path}`
- `form`: write a relative path separated by `/` that ends with `.wasm`, without `.` or `..`
- `hidden`: a name that starts with `.` is not part of a package

Component paths use visible relative names and the `.wasm` extension.

## E1003

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the component `{path}` is outside the {base}
- `root`: a component of a module under the root directory must be under the root directory
- `package`: a component of the package `{package}` must be under its `wasm` directory

Canonical component paths must remain within the allowed directory.

## E1004

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{path}` is not a WebAssembly component
- `not_wasm`: the file does not start with the WebAssembly magic bytes
- `core`: it is a core WebAssembly module; wrap it with `wasm-tools component new`
- `invalid`: the component is invalid: {reason}

External functions require binary WebAssembly components.

## E1005

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the component `{path}` imports {count}, so it cannot be called as a pure function
- `imports`: imports: {names}
- `target`: build it for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and wrap it with `wasm-tools component new`; `wasm32-wasip2` adds WASI imports

Only components without imports can provide pure external functions, including calls through generated adapters.

## E1006

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the component `{path}` has no function `{name}`
- `exports`: the functions it exports are {names}
- `version`: the component exports the interface as `{found}`; the version must match exactly
- `interface`: `{name}` is an interface; write `{name}#function`

External declarations name a function exported by the component, directly or as `interface#function`.

## E1007

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` of the component takes {found}, but `{function}` declares {expected}
- `declaration`: the component function corresponds to `{declaration}`

The declared parameter count must match the component function.

## E1008

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: argument {index} of `{function}` does not match the component
- Label: declared as `{declared}`
- `component`: the component expects `{wit}`
- `maps`: `{declared}` is passed as `{expected}`
- `reason`: {reason}
- `declaration`: the component function corresponds to `{declaration}`
- `user_type`: `{name}` here is the type declared in `{file}`, not `Benitoite.{name}.{name}`

Parameter types are checked by position against their WIT representations.

## E1009

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the result of `{function}` does not match the component
- Label: declared as `{declared}`
- `component`: the component returns `{wit}`
- `maps`: `{declared}` is passed as `{expected}`
- `reason`: {reason}
- `declaration`: the component function corresponds to `{declaration}`
- `user_type`: `{name}` here is the type declared in `{file}`, not `Benitoite.{name}.{name}`

The result type must match its WIT representation.

## E1010

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: `{ty}` cannot be passed to or from an external function in this version
- `types`: the types that can be passed are Integer, Integer8, Integer16, Integer32, Float, Float32, Boolean, Character, String, Byte, UnsignedInteger16, UnsignedInteger32, UnsignedInteger64, Bytes, List, Map, Set[D] as flags when D is a data type with 1 to 32 constructors that take no arguments, Option, Result, Pair, Triple, records and `data` types with concrete type arguments that are not recursive (including a single-constructor data type passed as a tuple), and Unit as a result
- `recursive`: recursive types cannot be passed, including recursion through List or other types
- `recursive_declaration`: the dependency cycle includes the declaration of `{recursive_name}`
- `flags_count`: flags require a data type with 1 to 32 constructors; empty selections are allowed
- `flags_data`: flags require Set[D], where D is a concrete data type and every constructor takes no arguments
- `map_key`: map keys must be Boolean, an integer of any supported width, Character, or String
- `budget`: types deeper than 100 cannot match any WIT type; larger types are not checked (100,000 expanded nodes per type, 1,000,000 per check); declaration dependency visits also count toward the per-check limit
- `adapter_preparation`: external function `{name}` cannot prepare its generated adapter within the type-walk budget
- `adapter_preparation_budget`: adapter preparation allows 4,000,000 type-node visits per declaration, separately from WIT matching
- `declaration_budget`: external function `{name}` is not checked because the total type expansion budget is exhausted
- `declaration`: external declaration `{name}`
- `user_type`: `{name}` here is the type declared in `{file}`, not `Benitoite.{name}.{name}`

External functions accept only the supported concrete types.

## E1011

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` of the component `{path}` is asynchronous

External functions must be synchronous in this version.

## E1012

- Kind: check (error)
- Message: the component `{path}` has no resource `{name}`
- `exports`: exported resources: {names}

External types name an exported resource of the component.

## W0301

- Kind: check (warning)
- Message: `{name}` is deprecated
- Label: deprecated
- `declared`: declared deprecated here
- `message`: {message}

The declaration is marked `@deprecated` and may be removed later. The note shows its message.

## W0401

- Kind: check (warning)
- Message: this divides by zero
- Label: the divisor is always 0

The divisor is a constant expression whose value is 0, so the division stops the program when it runs.

## W0402

- Kind: check (warning)
- Message: this calculation overflows `{ty}`
- Label: always overflows

Every operand is a constant expression and the result does not fit the type, so the calculation stops the program when it runs.

## W0403

- Kind: check (warning)
- Message: the key `{key}` appears more than once
- Label: repeated key
- `first`: first given here

`Map.fromList` keeps the last value for a repeated key and `Set.fromList` keeps one element, so a repeated key in a list literal is likely a mistake.

## W0501

- Kind: check (warning)
- Message: `uses IO.All` allows more effects than this function performs
- `narrow`: write `uses {effects}`
- `remove`: remove `uses IO.All`; this function performs no effects

Listing only the effects a function performs shows which operations it needs.

## R0101

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: division by zero

Integer and Decimal division, `mod`, `Integer.floorDivide`, and `Integer.floorModulo` by zero stop the program.

## R0102

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: integer overflow

The result does not fit in a 64-bit signed integer.

## R0103

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: Decimal overflow

The result does not fit in a `Decimal` even after rounding.

## R0201

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: failed to write to standard output
- `reason`: {reason}

Writing to standard output failed, for example because the reading side of a pipe was closed.

## R0202

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: failed to write to standard error
- `reason`: {reason}

Writing to standard error failed.

## R0301

- Kind: args (error)
- Message: command-line argument {index} is not valid UTF-8

Arguments passed to a script must be valid UTF-8.

## R0401

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: failed to release `{resource}` opened at {location}
- Label: released here
- `failure`: failed to release `{resource}` opened at {location}: {reason}
- `reason`: {reason}

Releasing a resource failed when its `with` block ended, when its task was cancelled, or when a handler discarded the computation.

## R0402

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: `{resource}` is used after it was released

A resource cannot be used after its `with` block has ended.

## R0501

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: `resume` was called twice in one clause

A continuation can be resumed at most once.

## R0502

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: the handler for `{operation}` cannot be used in a task
- `clause`: the clause is here
- `tail`: a handler inherited by a task must end its clause with `resume`

Tasks inherit only handlers whose clauses end by calling `resume`.

## R0601

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: the external function `{function}` trapped: {trap}
- `component`: component `{component}`, function `{export}`

A WebAssembly trap or a Component Model ABI violation stops execution. Guest panics and Rust allocation failures can also become an unreachable trap.

## R0701

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: argument {index} of `{function}` is out of range

The function accepts only the values described in its documentation for this argument.

## R0801

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: a response was already sent for this request

`Http.respond` can be called once for each exchange.

## R0901

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: the call stack is too deep
- `frames`: {frames} calls were active
- `raise`: use tail calls, or raise the limit with `--max-call-stack`

Nested non-tail calls exceeded the call stack limit.

## R0902

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: `{function}` would create a value that is too large
- `size`: the result would have {size} {unit}; the limit is {limit}

A single operation cannot build a string or `Bytes` larger than 2^30 bytes, or a list longer than 2^24 elements.

## R0903

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: `{function}` read more than the limit of {limit} {unit}

A single read cannot produce a value larger than the size limit. Read the input in parts.

## R0904

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: the external function `{function}` used up its fuel limit of {limit}
- `component`: component `{component}`

Each external call has a default fuel limit of 10^10, independent of elapsed time. The user running the script can change it with `--wasm-fuel`.

## R0905

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: the external function `{function}` exceeded its {budget} limit of {limit} bytes
- `component`: component `{component}`
- `linear_memory`: total guest linear memory is limited to {limit} bytes per call, or over the lifetime of a stateful instance
- `adapter_allocation`: the external function `{function}` could not allocate generated adapter memory for {requested} bytes
- `adapter_memory`: the generated adapter allocator's memory.grow failed while reserving {requested} bytes, with {allocated} bytes already allocated; adapter memory also counts toward the Store's total linear-memory limit
- `adapter_store_memory`: this call uses generated adapter memory as well as guest memory; both count toward the Store's total linear-memory limit
- `adapter_memory32`: the generated adapter allocator requested {requested} bytes, exceeding the memory32 address limit of {limit} bytes
- `transfer`: values passed to or from an external function are limited to {limit} bytes in their host representation, in each direction

By default, external calls limit total guest linear memory to 64 MiB and each direction of value transfer to a 256 MiB budget. Generated adapters count the complete transfer buffer and separately limit logical value construction to the same budget. The user running the script can change these limits with `--wasm-memory` and `--wasm-transfer`.

## R0906

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: the external function `{function}` needed {size} {resource}; the limit is {limit}
- `component`: component `{component}`

Each external call limits core instances, memories, and tables to 16 each, and each guest table to 10,000 elements. Reduce the component's resource requirements.

## R0907

- Kind: resource (error)
- Message: `{function}` could not reserve buffer memory
- `capacity`: the requested buffer capacity was {requested_bytes} bytes

The logical length was within the value size limit, but the host could not reserve the requested buffer capacity. This is not a process-wide memory usage measurement.

## R1001

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: no task can proceed because tasks are waiting for each other

Every remaining task waits for another task, so the program cannot continue.

## R1002

- Kind: runtime (error)
- Message: the awaited task was cancelled, so it has no result

`Task.await` cannot return a value for a task that was cancelled. A `Task` value used outside its `with` block may refer to such a task.

## L0101

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` needs too many registers
- `limit`: a function can use at most 65535 registers; split it into smaller functions

The bytecode addresses registers with 16 bits.

## L0102

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` has too many constants
- `limit`: a function can have at most 65536 constants; split it into smaller functions

The bytecode addresses constants with 16 bits.

## L0103

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` has too many `match` expressions
- `limit`: a function can have at most 65536 switch tables; split it into smaller functions

The bytecode addresses the switch tables of a function with 16 bits.

## L0104

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the function `{name}` has too many `handle` expressions
- `limit`: a function can have at most 65536 handlers; split it into smaller functions

The bytecode addresses the handler descriptions of a function with 16 bits.

## L0105

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the program has too many constructors
- `limit`: a program can have at most 65535 constructors

The bytecode addresses constructors with 16 bits.

## L0106

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the program uses too many built-in functions
- `limit`: a program can use at most 65535 built-in functions

The bytecode addresses built-in functions with 16 bits.

## L0107

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the program has too many implementations
- `limit`: a program can have at most 65535 implementations

The bytecode addresses implementations with 16 bits.

## L0108

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the program has too many effect operations
- `limit`: a program can have at most 65535 effect operations

The bytecode addresses effect operations with 16 bits.

## L0109

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the trait `{name}` has too many methods
- `limit`: a trait can have at most 65535 methods

The bytecode addresses the methods of a trait with 16 bits.

## L0110

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the trait `{name}` has too many supertraits
- `limit`: a trait can have at most 65535 supertraits

The bytecode addresses the supertraits of a trait with 16 bits.

## L0111

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: an implementation of `{name}` has too many constraints
- `limit`: an implementation can have at most 65535 constraint dictionaries

The bytecode addresses the dictionaries of an implementation with 16 bits.

## L0113

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the program uses too many external functions
- `limit`: a program can use at most 65535 external functions

The bytecode addresses external functions with 16 bits.

## L0112

- Kind: limit (error)
- Message: the definition `{name}` is too large to compile
- `definition_final`: the final match decisions in this definition exceed their node or edge budget; split it into smaller functions
- `nodes`: the final match decision exceeds its node budget; split it into smaller matches
- `edges`: the final match decision exceeds its edge budget; split it into smaller matches
- `table`: the match decision requires more than 64 MiB of working tables; simplify the match
- `instructions`: the definition requires more than 4,194,304 generated instructions; split it into smaller functions

The compiler shares match decisions and falls back to matching rows in source order; final decision nodes, edges, working tables, and generated instructions remain bounded.

{"byteLength":14402,"contentHash":{"algorithm":"sha256","value":"796a618ba8438e1b70b8382c58110058e2790edce879c965f1872b3c431dd453"},"kind":"skillDocument","name":"references/grammar.md","producer":{"build":{"commit":"e6247c11712466a387e46d16147dcc819e6e797a","dirty":null,"provenance":{"commit":"git","dirty":"notCollected"},"target":"aarch64-apple-darwin"},"name":"benitoite","version":"0.0.10"},"schemaVersion":1,"text":"# Benitoite grammar

The base grammar of Benitoite in EBNF. `{ ... }` means zero or more repetitions, `[ ... ]` means optional, and `|` separates alternatives. `NL` is a line break that separates items. `CommaList(X)` is a comma-separated list of `X` that may be empty and may end with a comma; `LineList(X)` is a list of `X` separated by line breaks.

Identifiers exclude the 36 keywords listed in [Keywords as names](common-mistakes.md#keywords-as-names), except that `record` is also accepted where a lowercase name is required (including parameters, labels, bindings, and value references). `die` cannot be a name, including in labels, fields, import aliases, and names after a dot. It is accepted only as a failure action of `try`, not as a standalone expression. `fn`, `pub`, `impl`, `mut`, `async`, `await`, `spawn`, and `select` remain ordinary identifiers. `as`, file-header words, built-in constraint names, and attribute names are read specially only in their own contexts. `extensible` is an ordinary identifier. The argument-free `@extensible` attribute applies to data and record declarations. Outside their defining package, patterns must cover future shapes with an unguarded variable or `_`. The argument-free `@opaque` attribute applies to public or package-public data and record declarations. It exposes the type and ordinary values while restricting constructors, record updates, representation patterns, and field accessors to the declaring module. Other modules of the same package are outside this boundary; use public construction and inspection functions.

A physical line break immediately after `return` always ends the statement, even inside parentheses or before an operator on the next line. Comments and blank lines do not change this rule. For an ordinary `return`, start the required value on the same physical line (otherwise E0201). Once the value has started, ordinary multiline continuation is allowed after operators, inside parentheses or call arguments, and after `then`. A short lambda must still fit on one physical line.

`try e or return` explicitly returns a failure to the caller, with the same types and evaluation as bare `try e`. Bare try is permanently fixed to returning failure; it never infers an exit. Prefer explicit return in reusable functions, libraries, and callbacks, and die in entry points that should end the run. Neither returning form requires Show. The return action takes no value. `TryOperand` includes the whole expression, including pipes, but stops before `or return` or `or die` at the same depth. A nested `try` takes its own action first; parentheses, arguments, lambdas, and blocks have their own expression boundaries. Other `or` expressions stay Boolean operators. Line breaks before and after `or` continue the expression; a line break immediately after the action's `return` ends it, even inside parentheses. Put a comma or closing delimiter on that same line. Parenthesize an explicit try before continuing it with an operator, call, or type application: `(try r or return) + 1`. The formatter preserves bare and explicit forms.

`try e or die` and `try e or die(message)` keep the enclosing return type unrestricted and add `Process.Exit`. Import `Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process` to write `uses Process.Exit`; the internal dependency does not import that name. Result errors require `Trait.Show`; Option does not. The optional message must be a pure String. Success evaluates neither message nor Show. Failure evaluates the message, then Show (or a fixed cause for None), then `Process.exit(1)`. Start the message's opening parenthesis on the same physical line as `die`. Outside parentheses, a line break after `die` or its message ends the statement. Direct `return`, `try`, and outer `resume` are forbidden in the message; a lambda written there has its own return boundary. A short lambda must include the entire message on its physical line. The default exit cancels remaining tasks, releases resources, transfers output, then reports the source location, optional message, and cause once, with status 1. No Console.Write is required for this host report. Release and flush failures follow as supplements without changing status 1. A Process.Exit handler receives the ordinary exit code; the handled call's report is discarded and never attached to a later exit. A test using die fails and the runner continues with the next test. Purity does not guarantee termination of message or Show, and static checking does not guarantee intended results or success of external operations.

A short lambda contains exactly one statement, and the entire lambda (including its header and any nested syntax) must fit on one physical line. Its expression uses the ordinary precedence; outer commas, closing delimiters, branch/block boundaries, and the end of the line or file end it. Use `return` to return a value. For a multiline body, start the body on the line after the header and close it with `end lambda`. A body starting on the header's last line takes an explicit `end lambda` only immediately after its statement on that same physical line. It never takes a terminator on a later line; blank lines do not affect which lambda a terminator closes. When either lambda in a directly nested pair omits its terminator, parenthesize the inner lambda. Call arguments and binding statements provide independent boundaries. Prefer the short form for a one-statement body; explicit terminators are valid and the formatter preserves the chosen form. Before adding another statement, start the body after the header and add `end lambda`.

For selecting a value or action, prefer `match`. Use `if` without `else` for conditional work or an early return. `else`, `else if`, and `shadow` are valid but are discouraged; these recommendations add no warnings. Prefer a fresh `bind` name for each new value. Preserve condition evaluation count and order, evaluate only the selected branch, and keep the target of `return`; nest boolean matches for effectful conditions instead of moving them into guards. For a final catch-all branch, prefer an ordinary binding name such as `other` or `otherCode` that does not collide with outer local names or visible constants, and put no unreachable branch after it. `case _ ->` is valid. This advice does not apply to `_` inside constructors, discarded bindings, or partial applications.

Function types require a name for every parameter. Ordinary functions with two or more parameters require named arguments; single-parameter functions accept either positional or named arguments. Parameter names must match even for a single positional higher-order argument. Ordinary calls accept named values such as `f(b: readB(), a: readA())`. Labels name parameters; they do not refer to local variables. The callee is evaluated first, then argument expressions in source order; only the saved values are placed in declaration order. Unknown, repeated, missing, or mixed named/positional arguments are errors. Function-type parameter names and lambda parameter names must match the contract; names are never inferred from the order of call labels. Direct data constructors use positional fields, while record construction uses named fields. Calls through an unannotated parameter wait for a known contract from constraints in the same function body. If the names and order remain unknown, E0455 requires a function-type annotation with parameter names, even for an unused lambda or a single positional argument. Contracts are not generalized or supplied later by callers of an already checked function. Named holes preserve the original parameter names in source order: `f(b: _, a: _)` creates a `function(b: B, a: A) -> R`. The callee and fixed arguments run inside that generated function, when it is called; `return` and `try` target it, and `resume` cannot cross its boundary. A pipe first evaluates its left side once, then its right callee and explicit arguments. Without direct holes it supplies parameter 0: `xs |> List.map(f: action)`. Explicitly supplying that parameter is a duplicate; remaining parameters require labels. With direct holes, or a parenthesized right side, the pipe instead calls the resulting function with one argument. It never fills an arbitrary free position or automatically partially applies a function. Constructor values use `arg1`, `arg2`, etc.; record constructor values use field names. Direct constructor holes keep their original position names.

Working programs for common tasks. Copy one and change it. Every example is checked against the current `benitoite`.

All examples import the IO modules under `Benitoite.Unofficial`, because those modules are unofficial in this release.

## Contents

- [Program shape and error handling](#program-shape-and-error-handling)
- [Calls, callback contracts, holes, and pipes](#calls-callback-contracts-holes-and-pipes)

- [CSV](#csv)

- [HTTP](#http)
- [Collections](#collections)
- [Concrete and generic containers](#concrete-and-generic-containers)

- [Numeric widths and conversions](#numeric-widths-and-conversions)
- [WASM external functions and WIT types](#wasm-external-functions-and-wit-types)

## Concrete and generic containers

Prefer concrete functions when the container is known: `List.map/fold`, `Option.map/andThen`, and `Result.map/andThen/mapError`. For a function shared by multiple containers, require the smallest class that provides the operations used. `Functor` supplies map, `Applicative` adds pure/apply, and `Monad` adds flatMap. Their two-parameter counterparts preserve the second type of `F[A, X]`. Import `Benitoite.Trait` to name the classes; `Result` itself stays in the prelude.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Trait
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function twice[F[_, _]: Trait.Functor2, X](x: F[Integer, X]) -> F[Integer, X]
  return Trait.Functor2.map(x: x, f: lambda(value) return value * 2 end lambda)
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind concrete: Result[Integer, String] <- Result.map(r: Result.Ok(3), f: lambda(value) return value * 2 end lambda)
  bind generic: Result[Integer, String] <- twice(Result.Ok(3))
  Console.writeLine(Integer.toString(Result.unwrapOr(r: concrete, fallback: 0)))
  Console.writeLine(Integer.toString(Result.unwrapOr(r: generic, fallback: 0)))
end function
```

```output
6
6
```

`Trait.Monad2` includes `Applicative2` and `Functor2`, so a function that also needs flatMap can use its inherited map. The standard implementation is `Result`; a user-defined two-parameter data type can implement the same classes. `Applicative2.pure` may need a result annotation such as `Result[Integer, String]` to determine the error type. `Applicative2.apply` prefers an error in `fs` to an error in `x`, and calls the wrapped function once only when both are Ok. Both argument expressions still run in source order. When writing its type, keep the parentheses in `Result[(function(value: A) -> B uses E), X]` to separate the effect row from `X`.

There is no partial application of type constructors: `Result` cannot be passed to a one-parameter `Monad` or `Traversable`. A fully applied transparent alias is expanded as usual; a bare alias is not a separate type constructor or a way to select another dictionary.

Use `andThen/flatMap` to pass a successful value to another computation with the same error type; use `Result.mapError` to align error types explicitly. `try … or return` returns a failure to the caller; `or die` reports it and ends the run. `Failure.toResult` handles typed Fail and returns a value, removing the handled Fail from the enclosing `uses` bound. Choose display, comparison, and combination functions by meaning: `Show` can quote text and is not numeric `toString`, and `Order[Float]` defines a total order including NaN that differs from built-in comparisons.

## Program shape and error handling

Use `or return` in a reusable function, library, or callback, and `or die` in an entry point that should report a failure and end the run. This example preserves the error in `load` and uses it as the cause of an exit in `main`.

```files
name: input.txt
ready
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function load(path: String) -> Result[String, IOError] uses File.Read
  return Result.Ok(try File.readText(path) or return)
end function

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind text <- try load("input.txt") or die("could not read input.txt")
  Console.write(text)
end function
```

```output
ready
```

`load` preserves the original IOError for its caller. `main` uses the standard Show implementation if loading fails, so it needs no conversion solely for display. Adding Process.Exit changes the function's contract; review the action, return type, and effects together.

`try e or die` and `try e or die(message)` accept a standard `Result[T, E]` or `Option[T]` and produce `T` on success, without restricting the enclosing function's return type. They add `Process.Exit`; import `Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process` to name it in `uses`. The module cannot be renamed with `as` (E0339), so write `uses Process.Exit`. The compiler connects the standard Show and exit references internally, but does not import names into your scope. No `Console.Write` effect is required for the host's failure report.

| Action | Enclosing return type | Display requirement | Additional effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bare try or `or return` | `Result[U, E]` or `Option[U]`, matching the input | None | None |
| `or die` or `or die(message)` | Any | `Trait.Show` for Result's error type; none for Option | `Process.Exit` |

The input is evaluated once. Success evaluates neither the message nor Show. Failure evaluates the optional pure `String` message once, then the error's Show once, then calls the standard exit operation with status 1. A message does not implicitly bind the error to a name. Direct `return`, `try`, and outer `resume` are forbidden in the message; a lambda written there has its own return boundary. `IOError`, `NetworkError`, `Json.ParseError`, and `Csv.ParseError` already implement Show by returning their `message` string unchanged. Implement Show for another error type, or use `Result.mapError` to convert it to a type with Show. The returning forms need no Show.

A String cause retains Show's quotes and escapes. Option.None has the fixed cause `expected a value, got Option.None`. The message is displayed as plain text, and an empty message is distinct from no message; neither removes the cause. If the message or Show stops with a runtime error or resource failure, that stop is used instead of a die report. Purity and static checking do not guarantee termination, the intended result, or success of external operations.

The default exit ends the whole run, including when called by a child task: remaining tasks are cancelled, resources are released, and buffered output is transferred. The CLI then reports `error: explicit failure exit`, the source location, an optional `message: ...`, and a `cause: ...` once to standard error. Release and final output failures follow as supplementary reports and keep status 1. With `--diagnostics=json`, the die report has `kind: "die"`, `code: null`, and the same location and notes. Cancellation does not undo external work already started. Competing exits, interruption, and internal errors follow the ordinary stop rules; only the adopted die carries this report.

A language handler can replace the existing `Process.Exit` operation; it receives only the usual exit code, and the handled call's report is discarded rather than attached to a later exit. In `benitoite test`, die fails that test and the runner continues with the next one. Text and JSON preserve its cause, message, and location without adding a second copy to captured output. Use `Process.exit(code)` for an arbitrary exit status.

The input includes pipes up to `or return` or `or die` at the same depth; ordinary Boolean `or` stays an operator. Parenthesize an explicit try before adding an operator or call, as in `(try parsePort(text) or die) + 1`. `or return` takes no value. A physical newline immediately after its `return` ends the statement. Start a message's `(` on the same physical line as `die`; outside parentheses, a newline after `die` or its message ends the statement. A short lambda must include its whole action and message on one physical line. The formatter preserves bare and explicit forms.

The following example instead makes returning `Result[Unit, String]` the contract of `main`. When it returns `Result.Error(message)`, the message is reported and the exit code is 1. `or return` (with the same meaning as bare try) returns early with the error.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function parsePort(text: String) -> Result[Integer, String]
  return match Integer.parse(text) with
    case Option.Some(n) if n > 0 and n < 65536 -> Result.Ok(n)
    case otherPort -> Result.Error("not a port: ${text}")
  end match
end function

function main() -> Result[Unit, String] uses Console.Write
  bind port <- try parsePort("8080") or return
  Console.writeLine("port ${port}")
  bind other <- try parsePort("http") or return
  Console.writeLine("never printed ${other}")
  return Result.Ok(())
end function
```

```output
port 8080
exit 1
```

```stderr
not a port: http
```

Use `Process.exit(code)` (effect `Process.Exit`) only when a specific exit code is needed.

Import `Benitoite.Unofficial.Failure` to use typed failures. `Failure.fromResult(result)`
returns Ok's value or raises the original error. `Failure.toResult(body)` calls body
once and returns `Result[T, E]`, keeping effects other than `Failure.Fail[E]`.
The callback's remaining row must exclude Fail; this condition comes from the
signature. Neither conversion requires Show or equality. Annotate the result binding
or callback type if E cannot be inferred; function calls have no explicit type arguments.

An E0506 on standard Fail can be fixed with toResult inside main or the @test
function. Remove the handled Fail from the entry's uses and retain other effects.
Result.andThen/flatMap only chains Result values; it does not handle Fail. The
toResult help does not apply to Log or a user-defined effect with the same name.

Place toResult outside List.map to stop the entire map at the first raised failure.
Its non-resumable clause skips the remaining computation and releases nested with
scopes from inner to outer, once each. Release failures remain runtime errors.
A normal return or try from the callback returns to toResult, which wraps that value
in Ok, including a returned Result. Put toResult inside each child task to return a
Result through Task.all/allOk; a child cannot use a parent's non-resumable handler
(R0502). Handle a failure inside a lazy body to cache a Result; an unhandled Fail
makes that body impure (E0503). The conversions do not catch die, Process.Exit,
runtime errors, resource limits, interruption, cancellation, or external traps.

## Calls, callback contracts, holes, and pipes

For an ordinary call with two or more parameters, label every argument with its declared name. A one-parameter call may omit its label; a zero-parameter call uses `f()`. Labels can appear in any order. The callee is evaluated first, then each argument once in source order.

Parameter names belong to function types. A callback must have exactly the expected names in the expected order, including unused parameters. `List.map` expects `value`, while `Integer.toString` declares `n`; use an explicit wrapper to adapt it. `List.fold` expects `acc, value`; Map callbacks commonly expect `key, value`. Read the full declaration in `stdlib/<Module>.md`. A descriptive alias can be bound inside a multiline lambda without changing its contract.

Holes retain their target parameter names in the order written. A pipe without direct holes supplies the first declared parameter and requires labels for the remaining arguments. With direct holes, or a parenthesized right side, it calls the resulting function with one argument. Constructor values use positional names `arg1`, `arg2`, etc.; record constructor values use field names and record accessors take `value`.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function subtract(a: Integer, b: Integer) -> Integer
  return a - b
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind xs <- [1, 2, 3]
  bind doubled <- List.map(xs: xs, f: lambda(value) return value * 2)
  bind labels <- doubled |> List.map(f: lambda(value) return Integer.toString(value))
  Console.writeLine(labels |> String.join(separator: ","))
  bind swapped: function(b: Integer, a: Integer) -> Integer <- subtract(b: _, a: _)
  Console.writeLine("${swapped(b: 2, a: 9)}")
  bind make <- Pair
  bind pair <- make(arg1: 4, arg2: "four")
  Console.writeLine("${Pair.first(pair)} ${Pair.second(pair)}")
end function
```

```output
2,4,6
7
4 four
```

For E0454, compare callback names position by position. For E0455, annotate the function parameter with a named function type; call-label order cannot determine its contract. Direct constructors, patterns, attributes, handler bindings, and `resume` keep their own syntax.

## Reading and writing files

`File.readText` reads a whole file; `File.readLines` reads it as lines. Relative paths are resolved against the directory where `benitoite` was started.

```files
name: input.txt
apple 3
banana 5
cherry 7
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, File.Write, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind lines <- try File.readLines("input.txt") or die
  bind total <- List.fold(xs: lines, initial: 0, f: lambda(acc, value)
    return match String.split(s: value, separator: " ") with
      case [_, count] -> acc + Option.unwrapOr(o: Integer.parse(count), fallback: 0)
      case otherFields -> acc
    end match
  end lambda)
  bind report <- "lines: ${List.length(lines)}\ntotal: ${total}\n"
  bind _ <- try File.writeText(path: "report.txt", text: report) or die
  bind _ <- try File.appendText(path: "report.txt", text: "done\n") or die
  Console.write(try File.readText("report.txt") or die)
  return ()
end function
```

```output
lines: 3
total: 15
done
```

A missing file is an `IOError` value, not a crash. Match on the `Result` to handle it.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, Console.Write
  return match File.readText("missing.txt") with
    case Result.Ok(text) -> Console.write(text)
    case Result.Error(error) ->
      match IOError.kind(error) with
        case IOErrorKind.NotFound -> Console.writeLine("missing.txt does not exist")
        case otherKind -> Console.writeLine("could not read: ${IOError.message(error)}")
      end match
  end match
end function
```

```output
missing.txt does not exist
```

Listing a directory and checking for a file:

```files
name: notes.md
# notes
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, File.Write, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind _ <- try File.createDirectory("out") or die
  bind names <- try File.listDirectory(".") or die
  List.forEach(xs: List.sort(names), f: lambda(value) Console.writeLine(value))
  bind found <- try File.exists("notes.md") or die
  Console.writeLine(match found with
    case true -> "notes.md exists"
    case false -> "no notes.md"
  end match)
  return ()
end function
```

```output
main.bnt
notes.md
out
notes.md exists
```

## JSON

`Json.parse` returns a `Json.Value`. Read fields with `Json.get` and the `Json.as...` functions, which return `Option`.

```files
name: orders.json
[
  {"category": "book", "amount": 1200},
  {"category": "food", "amount": 300},
  {"category": "book", "amount": 800}
]
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Json

function amountOf(order: Json.Value) -> Result[Pair[String, Integer], String]
  bind category <- Option.andThen(o: Json.get(value: order, k: "category"), f: Json.asString)
  bind amount <- Option.andThen(o: Json.get(value: order, k: "amount"), f: Json.asInteger)
  return match Pair(category, amount) with
    case Pair(Option.Some(c), Option.Some(a)) -> Result.Ok(Pair(c, a))
    case otherFields -> Result.Error("an order needs a category and an amount")
  end match
end function

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind text <- try File.readText("orders.json") or die
  bind parsed <- try Json.parse(text) or die
  bind orders <- try Option.okOr(o: Json.asArray(parsed), error: "orders.json is not an array") or die
  bind totals <- List.fold(xs: orders, initial: Result.Ok(Map.empty()), f: lambda(acc, value)
    bind totalsMap <- try acc or return
    bind entry <- try amountOf(value) or return
    bind current <- Map.get(m: totalsMap, k: Pair.first(entry)) |> Option.unwrapOr(fallback: 0)
    return Result.Ok(Map.set(m: totalsMap, k: Pair.first(entry), value: current + Pair.second(entry)))
  end lambda)
  Map.forEach(m: try totals or die, f: lambda(key, value)
    Console.writeLine("${key}: ${value}")
  end lambda)
  return ()
end function
```

```output
book: 2000
food: 300
```

Build JSON with the constructors of `Json.Value` and write it with `Json.stringify` or `Json.stringifyPretty`. Object members are written in the order of their keys.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Json
```

## CSV

`Csv.parseWithHeader` reads the first row as the header and returns a map per row. Every field is a `String`; convert numbers with `Integer.parse` or `Decimal.parse`.

```files
name: scores.csv
name,score
Alice,90
"Bob, Jr.",75
Carol,82
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Csv
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function scoreOf(row: Map[String, String]) -> Integer
  return Option.andThen(o: Map.get(m: row, k: "score"), f: lambda(value) return Integer.parse(value)) |> Option.unwrapOr(fallback: 0)
end function

function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, File.Write, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind text <- try File.readText("scores.csv") or die
  bind rows <- try Csv.parseWithHeader(text) or die
  bind passed <- List.filter(xs: rows, p: lambda(value) return scoreOf(value) >= 80)
  bind output <- List.map(xs: passed, f: lambda(value)
    return [Option.unwrapOr(o: Map.get(m: value, k: "name"), fallback: ""), Integer.toString(scoreOf(value))]
  end lambda)
  bind csv <- Csv.format(List.prepend(xs: output, x: ["name", "score"]))
  bind _ <- try File.writeText(path: "passed.csv", text: csv) or die
  Console.write(csv)
  Console.write(Csv.format([["Bob, Jr.", "75"]]))
  return ()
end function
```

```output
name,score
Alice,90
Carol,82
"Bob, Jr.",75
```

## Running external commands

`Process.run` starts a program with a list of arguments, without a shell. Arguments are passed as they are: `$HOME` below is not expanded. A non-zero exit code is not an error; read it with `Process.Output.exitCode`.

`Process.run` and `Process.runAttached` reject explicitly supplied `Command.environment` names starting with `DYLD_` or `LD_`, ignoring ASCII case, before starting a child or arranging its pipes. This includes `LD_RUN_PATH` used by build tools, lowercase names, empty values, and resetting a variable to its inherited value. They return `Result.Error` with `IOErrorKind.InvalidInput`; the message names the first forbidden variable in lexical order of the original names, without its value. Existing checks for NUL, empty names, and `=` in names take precedence. This is an IO failure value, not a new static diagnostic. Handle it by reviewing and removing the explicit setting or choosing an operation compatible with the rule; do not bypass it by moving the variable to the parent's environment or wrapping the command in a shell.

The rule always applies on every OS, but does not remove inherited variables; `Process.shell` inherits them too. Accepting `Process.Run` permits `env` or a shell to set variables itself. The rule does not control the initial environment, `PATH`, command-specific settings, grandchildren, or every Windows DLL search. Use the harness or OS to enforce isolation.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function main() -> Unit uses Process.Run, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind printed <- try Process.run(Process.command(program: "echo", arguments: ["hello", "$HOME"])) or die
  Console.write(Process.Output.standardOutput(printed))
  bind sort <- Process.Command(..Process.command(program: "sort", arguments: []), environment: Map.fromList([Pair("LC_ALL", "C")]), input: Option.Some("pear\napple\n"))
  bind sorted <- try Process.run(sort) or die
  Console.write(Process.Output.standardOutput(sorted))
  bind failed <- try Process.run(Process.command(program: "sh", arguments: ["-c", "exit 3"])) or die
  Console.writeLine("exit code: ${Process.Output.exitCode(failed)}")
  return ()
end function
```

```output
hello $HOME
apple
pear
exit code: 3
```

`Process.shell` runs one command line with `/bin/sh -c`. Write only POSIX sh: no bash arrays, no `[[ ]]`, no `{a,b}` brace expansion, no `$'...'`. Prefer `Process.run` when no pipe or redirection is needed.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function main() -> Unit uses Process.Run, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind piped <- try Process.shell("printf 'b\\na\\nc\\n' | LC_ALL=C sort | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z'") or die
  Console.write(Process.Output.standardOutput(piped))
  bind checked <- try Process.shell("if [ -d / ]; then echo root; fi; echo oops >&2; exit 2") or die
  Console.write(Process.Output.standardOutput(checked))
  Console.write("stderr: ${Process.Output.standardError(checked)}")
  Console.writeLine("exit code: ${Process.Output.exitCode(checked)}")
  return ()
end function
```

```output
A
B
C
root
stderr: oops
exit code: 2
```

## HTTP

A client and a server in one program. The server listens on port 0 (the system picks a free port), serves a fixed number of requests in a task, and the client calls it. `with` releases its resources in reverse order when the block ends, and releasing a `TaskGroup` waits for all its tasks; if the server expects more requests than the client sends, the program waits forever at `end with`. Keep the two counts equal. Network effects are not part of `IO.All`; list them separately.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Json
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Network.Http

function route(request: Http.Request) -> Http.Response
  return match Pair(Http.Request.method(request), Http.pathSegments(Http.Request.path(request))) with
    case Pair("GET", ["hello", name]) -> Http.text(status: 200, s: "Hello, ${name}!")
    case Pair("GET", ["items"]) -> Http.json(status: 200, value: Json.Value.Array([Json.Value.Integer(1), Json.Value.Integer(2)]))
    case otherPath -> Http.text(status: 404, s: "not found")
  end match
end function

function serveLoop(listener: Http.Listener, remaining: Integer) -> Result[Unit, String] uses Http.Listen, State
  if remaining = 0 then return Result.Ok(()) end if
  bind exchange <- try Http.accept(listener) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return NetworkError.message(error)) or return
  bind _ <- try Http.respond(exchange: exchange, response: route(Http.requestOf(exchange))) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return NetworkError.message(error)) or return
  bind _ <- try Http.closeExchange(exchange) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return NetworkError.message(error)) or return
  return serveLoop(listener: listener, remaining: remaining - 1)
end function

function show(response: Http.Response) -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind body <- Option.unwrapOr(o: String.fromUTF8(Http.Response.body(response)), fallback: "(not UTF-8)")
  return Console.writeLine("${Http.Response.status(response)} ${body}")
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Http.Listen, Http.Connect, Console.Write, State, Process.Exit
  with listener = try Http.listen(host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0) or die,
    group = TaskGroup.open() do
    bind base <- "http://127.0.0.1:${Http.listenerPort(listener)}"
    bind server <- TaskGroup.spawn(group: group, action: lambda() return serveLoop(listener: listener, remaining: 3))
    bind hello <- try Http.get(base + "/hello/Ada") or die
    bind items <- try Http.get(base + "/items") or die
    bind request <- Http.ClientRequest(..Http.clientRequest(method: "POST", url: base + "/upload"), body: String.toUTF8("data"))
    bind missing <- try Http.send(request) or die
    bind _ <- try Task.await(server) or die
    List.forEach(xs: [hello, items, missing], f: lambda(value) show(value))
    return ()
  end with
end function
```

```output
200 Hello, Ada!
200 [1,2]
404 not found
```

A server that runs until it is stopped is simplest with `Http.serve`, which calls the handler for every request. (This example is only checked, not run, because it never ends.)

```benitoite check
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Network.Http

function respondTo(request: Http.Request) -> Http.Response
  return match Http.pathSegments(Http.Request.path(request)) with
    case [] -> Http.html(status: 200, s: "<h1>Home</h1>")
    case ["health"] -> Http.text(status: 200, s: "ok")
    case otherPath -> Http.text(status: 404, s: "not found")
  end match
end function

function main() -> Result[Unit, String] uses Http.Listen, State
  return Http.serve(host: "127.0.0.1", port: 8080, handler: respondTo) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return NetworkError.message(error))
end function
```

## Collections

Lists, maps, and sets are persistent: functions return new collections and never change the old one. Maps and sets are ordered by their keys, not by insertion order, so `Map.forEach` and `Set.toList` visit keys in sorted order.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind numbers <- List.range(start: 1, stop: 6)
  bind squares <- List.map(xs: numbers, f: lambda(value) return value * value)
  bind even <- List.filter(xs: squares, p: lambda(value) return value mod 2 = 0)
  Console.writeLine("${List.length(numbers)} numbers, sum ${List.fold(xs: numbers, initial: 0, f: lambda(acc, value) return acc + value)}")
  Console.writeLine(String.join(xs: List.map(xs: even, f: lambda(value) return Integer.toString(value)), separator: ", "))
  bind words <- String.split(s: "the cat saw the dog", separator: " ")
  bind counts <- List.fold(xs: words, initial: Map.empty(), f: lambda(acc, value)
    return Map.set(m: acc, k: value, value: Option.unwrapOr(o: Map.get(m: acc, k: value), fallback: 0) + 1)
  end lambda)
  Map.forEach(m: counts, f: lambda(key, value) Console.writeLine("${key}=${value}"))
  Console.writeLine(String.join(xs: Set.toList(Set.fromList(words)), separator: " "))
  return ()
end function
```

```output
5 numbers, sum 15
4, 16
cat=1
dog=1
saw=1
the=2
cat dog saw the
```

`List.range(start: start, stop: stop)` stops before `stop`. Lists have no index operator; use `List.get(xs: xs, i: i)`, which returns an `Option`.

Loops are written with recursion or with `List.forEach`, `List.map`, `List.fold`. A function that calls itself last (`return f(...)`) does not grow the stack.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function countDown(n: Integer, acc: List[String]) -> List[String]
  if n = 0 then return List.reverse(acc) end if
  return countDown(n: n - 1, acc: List.prepend(xs: acc, x: Integer.toString(n)))
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  return Console.writeLine(String.join(xs: countDown(n: 5, acc: []), separator: " "))
end function
```

```output
5 4 3 2 1
```

A mutable cell is a `Reference`; its functions need the effect `State`.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write, State
  bind counter <- Reference.new(0)
  List.forEach(xs: [3, 4, 5], f: lambda(value) Reference.set(reference: counter, value: Reference.get(counter) + value))
  return Console.writeLine("total ${Reference.get(counter)}")
end function
```

```output
total 12
```

Character ranges covering all Unicode scalars need no catch-all: use `case '\u{0}'..'\u{10ffff}' ->`, or split at `'\u{d7ff}'` and `'\u{e000}'`. This also applies inside records, constructors and lists, and to a full-range `bind` pattern. A following catch-all is unreachable (`E0602`); a redundant comma alternative uses `E0608`. Guards do not establish coverage, and Integer ranges still require a catch-all. A non-exhaustive character match reports a concrete missing scalar, such as `'\u{0}'` when only `'a'` is covered.

## Records and data types

A record has named fields. Read a field with `Type.field(value)`; make a changed copy with `Type(..value, field: new)`. A data type lists its constructors, which are always written with the type name.

Use the argument-free `@extensible` attribute on a data or record declaration when external patterns must also cover future shapes. Put it before `public` or `public(package)` if present. Inside its defining package, listing the current constructors can be exhaustive. Outside it, include an unguarded `case other ->` or `case _ ->`; a known constructor named `Other` does not cover future shapes. Guards do not count toward exhaustiveness. The rule applies through aliases and inside `Result`, `Option`, lists, and record fields. The package boundary is the same as for `public(package)`; a different module in the same package is still internal.

The standard failure types `IOErrorKind`, `NetworkErrorKind`, `Json.ParseError`, `Json.Codec.ConversionError`, and `Csv.ParseError` have this attribute. `Result` and `Option` remain closed; `Result.Error(error)` binds the whole error without decomposing it. For the two ParseError records, prefer `Json.ParseError.message(error)` or `Csv.ParseError.message(error)` to destructuring. A record pattern with `..` covers only the current shape, so an external `match` needs another variable or `_` branch (`E0601`), and a destructuring `bind` or `shadow` is rejected (`E0607`). Construction, updates, and getters still use the declared fields. The attribute does not promise compatibility for adding record fields.

Adding constructors to extensible data preserves external pattern exhaustiveness, but can change results, including by reclassifying a value formerly represented by `Other`. Removing or renaming constructors, or changing their fields, is outside this guarantee. Adding the attribute to a closed type can reject existing external patterns; removing it commits to a closed set and can make a branch unreachable. It does not let callers add constructors or change runtime tags, ABI, equality, or key constraints. WIT matching remains exact; the attribute does not allow unknown external tags.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

record Item
  name: String
  price: Integer
  quantity: Integer
end record

data Shape
  Circle(Float)
  Rectangle(Float, Float)
end data

function area(shape: Shape) -> Float
  return match shape with
    case Shape.Circle(r) -> 3.0 * r * r
    case Shape.Rectangle(w, h) -> w * h
  end match
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind item <- Item(name: "pen", price: 120, quantity: 3)
  bind more <- Item(..item, quantity: 10)
  Console.writeLine("${Item.name(more)}: ${Item.price(more) * Item.quantity(more)}")
  bind shapes <- [Shape.Circle(1.0), Shape.Rectangle(2.0, 3.5)]
  List.forEach(xs: shapes, f: lambda(value) Console.writeLine(Float.toString(area(value))))
  return ()
end function
```

```output
pen: 1200
3.0
7.0
```

## Writing tests

A test is a function with `@test("description")` that takes no arguments and returns `Unit` or `Result[Unit, String]`. A test that uses `try e or return` returns `Result[Unit, String]`; returning `Result.Error(message)` fails the test. Check results with `Assert.equal(actual: actual, expected: expected)` and `Assert.isTrue(condition: condition, message: message)` (effect `Assert.Check`). While editing, check without execution using `benitoite test --check file.bnt`. Immediately before confirmation, obtain one report with `benitoite test --check --report=json file.bnt`, review its effects including `Assert.Check`, then run with `benitoite test --allow-effects=<accepted names> file.bnt`; do not run `benitoite check` on a test file without `main`. See [Inspecting before execution](inspection.md) for the report and whole-run rejection rules.

```benitoite test
function slugify(title: String) -> String
  return String.join(xs: String.split(s: String.toLowercase(String.trim(title)), separator: " "), separator: "-")
end function

@test("slugify lowercases and joins words")
function slugifyJoins() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  Assert.equal(actual: slugify(" Hello World "), expected: "hello-world")
  Assert.isTrue(condition: String.contains(s: slugify("A B"), part: "-"), message: "the words are joined with -")
end function
```

Replace a built-in operation in a test with `handle ... with case Op(args) -> ...`. The handler runs instead of the real operation, so the test does not touch files or start commands. `resume(value)` returns `value` to the code that called the operation. Handling some operations of an effect does not remove the effect from the type, so the test still lists `File.Read` and `Process.Run` in `uses`. Functions whose type has `State` (`Reference`, `TaskGroup`, `Task.await`, the `close...` functions) cannot be handled in a `case`.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

function countWords(path: String) -> Result[Integer, String] uses File.Read
  bind text <- try File.readText(path) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return IOError.message(error)) or return
  return Result.Ok(List.length(List.filter(xs: String.split(s: text, separator: " "), p: lambda(value) return value <> "")))
end function

function gitBranch() -> Result[String, String] uses Process.Run
  bind output <- try Process.run(Process.command(program: "git", arguments: ["branch", "--show-current"])) |> Result.mapError(r: _, f: lambda(error) return IOError.message(error)) or return
  return Result.Ok(String.trim(Process.Output.standardOutput(output)))
end function

@test("countWords reads the file through File.readText")
function countWordsReadsFile() -> Unit uses Assert.Check, File.Read
  bind result <- handle
    countWords("notes.txt")
  with
    case File.readText(path) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: path, expected: "notes.txt")
      resume(Result.Ok("one two  three"))
  end handle
  Assert.equal(actual: result, expected: Result.Ok(3))
end function

@test("gitBranch runs git without starting it")
function gitBranchRunsGit() -> Unit uses Assert.Check, Process.Run
  bind result <- handle
    gitBranch()
  with
    case Process.run(command) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: Process.Command.program(command), expected: "git")
      resume(Result.Ok(Process.Output(exitCode: 0, standardOutput: "main\n", standardError: "")))
  end handle
  Assert.equal(actual: result, expected: Result.Ok("main"))
end function
```

## Numeric widths and conversions

Use the aliases `Integer`, `Float`, and `Byte` as the usual names. `Integer64`, `Float64`, and `UnsignedInteger8` are their canonical names, and `UnsignedInteger` is an alias of `UnsignedInteger64`. Aliases are the same type. The seven types (`Integer8`, `Integer16`, `Integer32`, `UnsignedInteger16`, `UnsignedInteger32`, `UnsignedInteger64`, and `Float32`) are distinct. All numeric types and modules are in the prelude; no import is needed.

Suffixes explicitly choose a width: `42s16`, `0xffu8`, `65535u16`, `18446744073709551615u64`, `1.5f32`. Unsuffixed values retain `Integer` or `Float`; the expected type never changes them. The suffix spelling is provisional and may change when the syntax is revised. Floating-point suffixes require a decimal point or exponent (`1.0f32`, not `1f32`). Only a directly applied minus sign includes the sign in signed-literal range checking: `-128s8` works, `-(128s8)` does not. Unsigned unary minus is forbidden even on zero. `Byte` has no arithmetic. `Integer8`, `Integer16`, `Integer32`, the unsigned integer types, `Byte`, and `Float32` cannot be constant or range patterns; use a bound name and a guard.

Range-checked conversions return `Option`; integer arithmetic overflow and division by zero stop execution. Narrow integer modules convert through `Integer`. `UnsignedInteger64.toInteger` returns `Option` because its upper half does not fit; `toDecimal` is exact over its whole range. `Float32.fromFloat` rounds and returns `None` when finite input becomes infinite; `Float32.toFloat` widens finite values exactly. Arithmetic rounds to binary32 after each operation. Read the corresponding generated module reference for every function's signature.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function smallInteger(text: String) -> Option[Integer16]
  bind value <- try Integer.parse(text) or return
  return Integer16.fromInteger(value)
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind value <- Option.unwrapOr(o: smallInteger("42"), fallback: 0s16)
  bind wide: UnsignedInteger <- 18446744073709551615u64
  Console.writeLine("${value + 1s16} ${smallInteger("32768") = Option.None}")
  Console.writeLine("${UnsignedInteger64.toDecimal(wide)} ${UnsignedInteger64.toInteger(wide) = Option.None}")
  Console.writeLine("${Float32.toFloat(1.5f32)} ${Byte.toInteger(255u8)}")
end function
```

```output
43 true
18446744073709551615 true
1.5 255
```

## WASM external functions and WIT types

Declare external functions without a body or `end function`, and check the component's actual WIT contract before calling. The component must be a binary, import-free Component Model component, with no WASI or host functions. Paths are relative to the root that owns the declaration; package components must be under `wasm/`. The export is a world function or `interface#function`, matching the full interface name including its version. The declaration is monomorphic and uses concrete types. Functions containing external resource types in their actual parameter/result fields need `uses State`; others are pure.

| Benitoite type | WIT correspondence |
|---|---|
| `Integer8`/`Integer16`/`Integer32`/`Integer` | `s8`/`s16`/`s32`/`s64` |
| `Byte`/`UnsignedInteger16`/`UnsignedInteger32`/`UnsignedInteger64` | `u8`/`u16`/`u32`/`u64` |
| `Float32`/`Float` | `f32`/`f64` |
| `Bytes`, `List[Byte]`; other lists, options, results | `list<u8>`; recursive correspondence to WIT list/option/result |
| Concrete records and `data` | Substitute type arguments, then match fields/cases in declaration order and normalized names |
| `Set[D]`, D with 1–32 argument-free constructors | `flags`; an empty selection is allowed |
| `Map[K, V]` | `map`; K is Boolean, an integer type, Character, or String; V is any supported type |
| `Pair`, `Triple`, or another single-constructor `data` with one or more arguments | `tuple` by argument position |
| A variant constructor with multiple arguments | One flat tuple payload, distributed back into those arguments |

Record/case names match after removing hyphens and lowercasing ASCII. Finite generic nesting is allowed; recursive declarations and unresolved type/effect variables are rejected. Functions, Decimal, ordinary Set types, tasks, and resources used with `with` cannot be passed. `Unit` is allowed only as an omitted function result or omitted side of a standard `Result`.

These declarations match the sample components used by the repository's `external/wit-docs-values` executable example:

```text
record Box[T]
  value: T
end record
@external("wasm", "generic.wasm", "box")
function box(v: Box[Integer]) -> Box[Integer]
@external("wasm", "generic.wasm", "nested")
function nested(v: Box[Box[Integer]]) -> Box[Box[Integer]]

data D1
  F1
end data
@external("wasm", "flags.wasm", "f1")
function f1(v: Set[D1]) -> Pair[Set[D1], Integer]

@external("wasm", "maps.wasm", "result")
function result(v: Map[String, Integer]) -> Map[String, Integer]

data Four
  Item(Integer, Integer, Integer, Integer)
end data
@external("wasm", "tuples.wasm", "tuple4")
function tuple4(v: Four) -> Four

data Two
  Value(Integer, Integer)
  Empty
end data
@external("wasm", "variants.wasm", "fields")
function two(v: Two) -> Two
```

The WIT shapes are a record with `value: s64`, a nested record, `flags { f1 }` with a tuple result, `map<string, s64>`, a four-element `tuple<s64, s64, s64, s64>`, and `variant { value(tuple<s64, s64>), empty }`. The sample guests return 42 from `box(Box(value: 35))`, inner value 0 from `nested(Box(value: Box(value: -7)))`, `Pair(Set.fromList([D1.F1]), 0)` from `f1(Set.empty())`, `Four.Item(12, 14, 16, 18)` from `tuple4(Four.Item(1, 2, 3, 4))`, and `Two.Value(14, 29)` from `two(Two.Value(3, 7))`. The sample `Map.toList(result(Map.empty()))` is `[Pair("a", 2), Pair("z", 3)]`: every returned entry is checked before normalization; duplicate keys keep the last value, and the final map is ordered by key. These numerical transformations are behavior of the sample guests.

The checker selects `typed`, `adapter`, `dynamic`, or `stateful` before execution, and does not retry after a failure. The `typed` route counts bytes and elements. Other supported values use a generated adapter; external resource types use the stateful dynamic route. Adapter generation or layout limits can select the dynamic route before calling. Generated and compiled code is shared within one execution, while pure calls each get a fresh Store.

Default limits are 10^10 fuel, 64 MiB total guest/adapter linear memory, 16 each of core instances/memories/tables, 10,000 elements per table, and 256 MiB transfer per direction. The adapter counts the entire packed argument/result sequences, including a 32-byte header and padding. Separately, the same `--wasm-transfer` value limits logical construction per direction: 16 bytes per language value occurrence plus string/Bytes contents. Bytes elements do not count as separate values; List[Byte] elements do. Map entries discarded by duplicate-key normalization still count. ABI-only grouping tuples do not add a language value. These limits do not bound total process memory. Adapter instructions consume fuel and respond to SIGINT/SIGTERM; `Task.withTimeout` cannot cancel an external call. String/Bytes/list size limits also apply.

Use `--wasm-stats` on `run` or `test` to inspect routes, fallback reasons, transfer, `construction_bytes` (the sum of both directions), and adapter failures. `--wasm-memory`, `--wasm-fuel`, and `--wasm-transfer` change limits without changing the function contract. Fuel exhaustion reports R0904, transfer/construction/memory exhaustion R0905, object limits R0906, and returned-value-size limits R0902. Traps and guest ABI violations report R0601; a declared `Result.Error` is an ordinary value. These runtime failures cannot be caught with `match` or `try`.

## Local construction and logging

Use a block to return the immutable snapshot while keeping its builder local. No State is added by the dedicated operations.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.StringBuilder
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind text <- block
    bind builder: StringBuilder <- StringBuilder.new()
    StringBuilder.appendAll(builder: builder, texts: ["hello", " world"])
    StringBuilder.copy(builder)
  end block
  Console.writeLine(text)
end function
```
```output
hello world
```

Use Log and SourceLocation from the prelude. Pass message, attributes and location explicitly; IO.All does not include Log. Use a complete handler or add Log to the accepted declared effects. For checked lengths/indices and nonempty lists, use the Range and NonEmptyList module references.
"}

Automatic commit lookup monitors existing HEAD, branch ref, packed-refs, and HEAD reflog files, not the index or working files. Changes outside those monitored files can go unnoticed. Change an explicit build input or clean-build the package to recollect information when needed. A build's commit and dirty values neither prove its complete source identity nor attest to executable trust.

Both inspection commands check without executing user functions, generating Benitoite bytecode, or starting a VM. Compile-time constant evaluation and static checks of external declarations still occur; a WASM component can be compiled for checking, without instantiation or calls. Inspection does not prove later code generation will fit the compiler's limits. `check` requires `main`; `test --check` does not. Test selection matches executing `test`: only tests declared in each selected entry count; imported tests do not. Direct files use their parent as root; directory discoveries share that directory's root, skip `package.bnt` and nested packages, and use lexical file order. Explicit paths keep argument order and duplicates.

| `kind` | `checkReport` for main, `testCheckReport` for tests; use `schemaVersion: 1` by default; `test --doc` uses version 2. |
| `producer` | `{name, version, build}`, matching the version query. |
| `executed` | Always `false`; no user function ran. |
| `targetsComplete` | Entry selection or discovery finished; this alone does not mean checks succeeded. |

An empty directory is a complete success with no targets and an empty aggregate. A failed file leaves other successful contracts available, but the overall `complete` is false and the aggregate is null. Discovery failure stops before any entry is checked; already discovered entries remain incomplete reference information. Usage errors have no inspected targets or sources. Imports, comments, strings, a handler operation name alone, and unrelated user functions named shell do not count. This is not reachability analysis: `present` does not prove invocation, and `absent` does not prevent external commands from starting a shell.

Sources include settings, dependencies, and embedded prelude sources, but exclude WASM binaries, files read only to verify dependency hashes, missing settings, directory observations, and sources whose full bytes were not retained. IDs are local to each report; repeated paths remain separate. Display paths cannot always be reversed to OS paths. Neither these hashes nor an inspection fixes the bytes used by a later run.

Inspection exits with 0 for `ok`, 2 for `checkError` or `usageError`, 3 for `internalError`, and 130 for an observed test-inspection interruption. `--deny-warnings` promotes warnings to check errors. Test inspection checks interruption before each file; a request during the last file may go unreported. Main inspection retains OS-default signal handling. Test-inspection status precedence is interruption, internal error, usage error, then check error. Write or flush failure exits with 1 and can leave incomplete output; initialization failures, aborts, forced termination, or failures outside the report boundary also need not return a report. Never accept an incomplete response.

`--allow-effects` accepts one comma-separated set of canonical atomic names, with `State`, `Log`, and `Assert.Check` included. Both `--allow-effects=<names>` and `--allow-effects <names>` work. Duplicate options or names, empty elements, whitespace, unknown or user-defined names, import aliases, `IO.All`, and `*` are usage errors. The newly checked declared bound must be a subset of the accepted set; extra allowed names are fine. Earlier check errors take precedence over comparison.
