`run` executes the same checked program whose bound was compared. With a limit, `test` prepares, compares, and compiles all entries before starting any test. If any entry fails preparation, none run. An effect limit compares static contracts; it does not restrict runtime operations or ensure intended results, termination, or successful IO. Different test entries can observe different dependency contents during preparation; all-input snapshot consistency is not guaranteed. Keep actual operations and resource isolation in the harness or OS.

To retrieve documentation without installing it:

```sh

benitoite skill show --format=json references/stdlib/IO.Process.md
```

`list` returns `schemaVersion: 1`, `kind: "skillList"`, `producer`, and a lexical `documents` array of `{name, byteLength, contentHash}`. `show` returns `schemaVersion: 1`, `kind: "skillDocument"`, `producer`, `name`, `byteLength`, `contentHash`, and `text`. For documentation examples, use `--doc` consistently on both inspection and execution:

How common constructs of Python, JavaScript, and Rust are written in Benitoite. Modules outside the prelude (`Console`, `File`, `Process`, `Json`, `Csv`, `Http`, ...) must be imported; see `stdlib/index.md` for their import names.

## Syntax

For failure propagation, Rust's `?` corresponds to `try result or return`: bare `try result` keeps this same returning meaning. To end a run with a cause, use `try result or die` with Process.Exit; it permits any enclosing return type and requires Show for the Result error. It is not an exception handler. See [Program shape and error handling](idioms.md#program-shape-and-error-handling).

| Python | JavaScript | Rust | Benitoite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `int` | `number` | `i64` | `Integer` |
| `float` | `number` | `f64` | `Float` |
| `str` | `string` | `String` | `String` |
| `bool` | `boolean` | `bool` | `Boolean` |
| `list[int]` | `number[]` | `Vec<i64>` | `List[Integer]` (type arguments use `[]`, never `<>`) |
| `dict[str, int]` | `Map<string, number>` | `BTreeMap<String, i64>` | `Map[String, Integer]` |
| `Optional[int]` | `number \| null` | `Option<i64>` | `Option[Integer]` |

| Python | JavaScript | Rust | Benitoite |
|---|---|---|---|

| `x = x + 1` (rebinding) | `let x; x = x + 1` | `let x = x + 1;` | `bind increased <- x + 1` (prefer a new name; `shadow` is valid but discouraged) |

| `match v:` / `case ...:` | `switch (v)` | `match v { p => e }` | `match v with` / `case p -> e` / `end match` |

| `and`, `or`, `not` | `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` | `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` | `and`, `or`, `not` |

| `Some`-like value | value | `Some(x)` | `Option.Some(x)` |

| `class P:` with fields | `{ name, age }` | `struct P { name: String }` | `record P` ... `end record` |
| `P(name="a")` | `{ name: "a" }` | `P { name: "a".into() }` | `P(name: "a")` |
| `p.name` | `p.name` | `p.name` | `P.name(p)` |

| `Enum` / tagged union | tagged object | `enum Shape { Circle(f64) }` | `data Shape` / `Circle(Float)` / `end data` |

For selecting values or actions, prefer `match`; use an `if` without `else` for conditional work or an early return. The table keeps `else if` to explain valid syntax, but it and `else` are discouraged. Preserve condition evaluation order and count, branch evaluation, and the target of `return`; nest boolean matches for effectful conditions. Prefer a fresh ordinary name for a final catch-all pattern; `_` inside constructors, in discarded bindings, and in partial applications is unaffected. Short lambdas must fit entirely on one physical line; multiline bodies start after the header and require `end lambda`. See `grammar.md` for terminator matching and nested lambdas.

Notes on numbers and ranges:

- `Integer` is 64-bit. Overflow stops the program with a runtime error (Python integers have no limit).
- `div` rounds toward zero and the sign of `mod` follows the dividend: `-7 div 2` is `-3` and `-7 mod 2` is `-1`. Python's `//` and `%` round down (`-7 // 2` is `-4`, `-7 % 2` is `1`); use `Integer.floorDivide` and `Integer.floorModulo` for that behavior.
- `div` or `mod` by 0 stops the program with a runtime error. `Float` division by 0 gives infinity or NaN.
- `Integer` has no `/`; convert with `Integer.toFloat` first when you need a fractional result.
- A range pattern `case 0..19` includes both ends (Rust `0..=19`). `List.range(start: 0, stop: 20)` excludes the upper end (Rust `0..20`, Python `range(0, 20)`).

There is no `null`, no exception, no mutable variable, and no loop statement. A function that performs IO lists its effects after `uses`.

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console

record Person
  name: String
  age: Integer
end record

function describe(p: Person) -> String
  bind group <- match Person.age(p) < 20 with
    case true -> "young"
    case false -> "adult"
  end match
  return "${Person.name(p)} (${group})"
end function

function main() -> Unit uses Console.Write
  bind ada <- Person(name: "Ada", age: 36)
  bind older <- Person(..ada, age: Person.age(ada) + 1)
  Console.writeLine(describe(older))
  Console.writeLine("${7 div 2} ${7 mod 2} ${Float.toString(7.0 / 2.0)}")
  Console.writeLine("${-7 div 2} ${-7 mod 2} ${Integer.floorDivide(a: -7, b: 2)} ${Integer.floorModulo(a: -7, b: 2)}")
  bind label <- match Person.age(older) with
    case 0..19 -> "teen or child"
    case n if n >= 65 -> "senior"
    case otherAge -> "working age"
  end match
  Console.writeLine(label)
  return ()
end function
```

```output
Ada (adult)
3 1 3.5
-3 -1 -4 1
working age
```

## Functions

For ordinary calls with two or more parameters, label every argument with its declared name; labels may be written in any order, but argument expressions run in source order after the callee. One-parameter calls can omit the label. Callback names and their order are part of the function type: `List.map` requires `function(value: T) -> U`, so an existing function with another parameter name needs a wrapper such as `lambda(value) return Integer.toString(value)`. `List.fold` requires `acc, value`; unused parameters keep their expected names. See `idioms.md` for holes, pipes, and generated names.

|---|---|---|---|
| `print(s)` | `console.log(s)` | `println!("{s}")` | `Console.writeLine(s)` (effect `Console.Write`) |
| `print(s, end="")` | `process.stdout.write(s)` | `print!("{s}")` | `Console.write(s)` |
| `sys.stderr.write(s)` | `console.error(s)` | `eprintln!("{s}")` | `Console.writeErrorLine(s)` |
| `input()` | `readline` | `stdin().read_line` | `Console.readLine()` (effect `Console.Read`) |
| `str(n)` | `String(n)` | `n.to_string()` | `Integer.toString(n)`, `Float.toString(x)` |
| `int(s)` | `parseInt(s)` | `s.parse::<i64>()` | `Integer.parse(s)` (returns `Option[Integer]`) |
| `float(n)` | `Number(n)` | `n as f64` | `Integer.toFloat(n)` |

| `s.split(",")` | `s.split(",")` | `s.split(',')` | `String.split(s: s, separator: ",")` |

Unlike passing an arbitrary environment map to a subprocess API, explicit `Process.Command.environment` settings cannot have names starting with `DYLD_` or `LD_` (ASCII case-insensitive), including `LD_RUN_PATH`, empty values, or same-value overwrites. Both `Process.run` and `Process.runAttached` return `IOErrorKind.InvalidInput` before starting a child. Inherited variables remain unchanged, including for `Process.shell`; accepting `Process.Run` still permits commands to set variables themselves. This is an input rule, not process isolation. See [Running external commands](idioms.md#running-external-commands).

Benitoite's declared effects can be inspected before execution: use `benitoite check --report=json main.bnt` or `benitoite test --check --report=json tests/`, then pass the reviewed atomic set to `run` or executing `test` with `--allow-effects=<names>`. Keep `Assert.Check` for tests. These are static upper bounds, not a sandbox or a promise of the intended result; the same set can permit different files or commands. A test-inspection report does not run tests. See [Inspecting before execution](inspection.md) for capability discovery and complete-result checks.

The same task in Benitoite, with the Python equivalent in comments:

```files
name: words.txt
the quick brown fox
jumps over the lazy dog
```

```benitoite
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Console
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.File
import Benitoite.Unofficial.IO.Process

// counts = {}
// for word in open("words.txt").read().split():
//     counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1
// for word in sorted(counts):
//     if counts[word] > 1: print(f"{word} {counts[word]}")
function main() -> Unit uses File.Read, Console.Write, Process.Exit
  bind text <- try File.readText("words.txt") or die
  bind words <- List.filter(xs: String.split(s: String.replace(s: text, old: "\n", new: " "), separator: " "), p: lambda(value) return value <> "")
  bind counts <- List.fold(xs: words, initial: Map.empty(), f: lambda(acc, value)
    return Map.set(m: acc, k: value, value: Option.unwrapOr(o: Map.get(m: acc, k: value), fallback: 0) + 1)
  end lambda)
  Map.forEach(m: Map.filter(m: counts, p: lambda(key, value) return value > 1), f: lambda(key, value)
    Console.writeLine("${key} ${value}")
  end lambda)
  Console.writeLine("${List.length(words)} words, ${Map.size(counts)} distinct")
  return ()
end function
```

```output
the 2
9 words, 8 distinct
```

Status: unofficial. Import it with `import Benitoite.Unofficial.Failure`. When the module becomes standard, the import name changes to `import Benitoite.Failure`.

Refer to its declarations as `Failure.<name>`, for example `Failure.fromResult`.

Typed, non-resumable failures. Import Benitoite.Unofficial.Failure explicitly.

An entry cannot leave Fail unhandled. Import Failure, catch it with toResult,
and remove the handled Fail from the entry's uses; other effects remain.
Result.andThen/flatMap chains Result values rather than catching Fail.

```benitoite error
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Failure
function main() -> Unit uses Failure.Fail[String]
  return Failure.raise("bad")
end function
```
```diagnostic
E0506
handle `Failure.Fail` with `handle ... with` inside `main`
or convert the failure with Failure.toResult inside `main`
```

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Failure
function work() -> Integer uses Failure.Fail[String]
  return Failure.raise("bad")
end function
@test
function failureExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  bind result: Result[Integer, String] <- Failure.toResult(body: lambda() return work() end lambda)
  Assert.equal(actual: result, expected: Result.Error("bad"))
end function
```

```text
Failure.raise[T, E]: function(error: E) -> T uses Failure.Fail[E]
```

The standard effect `Failure.Fail[E]` takes one error type. `Failure.raise` aborts to the nearest failure clause; `resume` is forbidden in that clause. A handle may contain either one failure clause or ordinary operation clauses. Catching removes only the body failure; a clause may raise a different error type. A row beside an explicit Failure.Fail in any part of a declared signature excludes failures (for example `Rest excludes Failure.Fail`). This condition is retained through higher-order values and modules, and is never inferred from a function body. Other effects take no type arguments. Handle every failure before main or a test returns. The error type requires neither Show nor equality.

```benitoite
public function fromResult[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> T uses Fail[E]
```

Returns the success value, or raises the original error without requiring Show.

```benitoite
public function toResult[T, E, effect Rest](body: function() -> T uses Fail[E], Rest) -> Result[T, E] uses Rest
```

Runs body once, returning Ok on success or Error when it raises a failure.
Rest excludes Fail; other effects and runtime stops keep their usual behavior.
"}

```benitoite test
    case Console.readLine() -> resume(Result.Ok(Option.Some("supplied")))

    case Console.readAllLines() -> resume(Result.Ok(["supplied"]))

    case Result.Ok(line) -> Assert.equal(actual: line, expected: Option.Some("supplied"))
```

Status: standard. Import it with `import Benitoite.ListBuilder`.

Function-local list construction. Import Benitoite.ListBuilder explicitly.
Declare with bind b: ListBuilder[T] <- ListBuilder.new(). Local operations add no effects; effects from ordinary arguments are preserved.
A builder is a second-class value: it cannot be stored in an ordinary variable,
returned from a function, or captured by a lambda or lazy expression.
Its kind name is not an ordinary type; builders cannot be ordinary function arguments.
Use copy to obtain an immutable List before capturing or storing a value.
Builders cannot cross lambda, lazy, partial-application, or handler-clause boundaries.
appendAll accepts previously prepared fragments; callbacks cannot capture the builder.

Status: unofficial. Import it with `import Benitoite.Unofficial.Network.Http`. When the module becomes standard, the import name changes to `import Benitoite.Network.Http`.

Refer to its declarations as `Http.<name>`, for example `Http.Listen`.

HTTP/1.1 servers without TLS and clients for http and https URLs.
The resource types `Listener` and `Exchange` are built in.
The server has no limit on the number of connections or the time a client may take to send a request.
Listen on 127.0.0.1, or put the server behind a reverse proxy; do not expose it to the internet directly.

```benitoite
public effect Listen
  /// Starts listening on `port` of `host`. Port 0 lets the operating system choose a free port.
  function listen(host: String, port: Integer) -> Result[Listener, NetworkError]
  /// Returns the port the listener listens on.
  function listenerPort(listener: Listener) -> Integer
  /// Waits for the next request and accepts it. Other tasks run while it waits.
  function accept(listener: Listener) -> Result[Exchange, NetworkError]
  /// Sends the response. Stops the program when called twice for one exchange.
  /// The status must be between 200 and 599. Sends no body for HEAD requests,
  /// statuses 204, 205, and 304, or 2xx responses to CONNECT requests.
  function respond(exchange: Exchange, response: Response) -> Result[Unit, NetworkError]
end effect
```

Listening for connections, accepting requests, and responding.

```benitoite
public effect Connect
  /// Sends the request and returns the response, including 4xx and 5xx responses.
  function send(request: ClientRequest) -> Result[Response, NetworkError]
end effect
```

```benitoite
public record Request
  method: String
  path: String
  query: List[Pair[String, String]]
  headers: List[Pair[String, String]]
  body: Bytes
end record
```

A request received by a server. Header names are in lowercase, in the order received.

Returns the request that was accepted. Stops the program when the exchange is closed or being closed.

Stops listening. A `with` binding closes the listener in the same way.


A `with` binding closes the exchange in the same way, ignoring failures.

Status: unofficial. Import it with `import Benitoite.Unofficial.NonEmptyList`. When the module becomes standard, the import name changes to `import Benitoite.NonEmptyList`.

Refer to its declarations as `NonEmptyList.<name>`, for example `NonEmptyList.NonEmptyList`.

An opaque nonempty list. Construction checks once; head returns an element and tail may be empty.
The wrapper retains its elements and shares any Reference values they contain. Import this module explicitly.
When the element type supports equality, = compares both stored fields, first and rest, structurally. Assert failure output shows these internal field names and values. Their automatic accessors remain private; use head and tail. The wrapper does not implement Trait.Show.
When the element type is a key type, the wrapper is a key type and can be a Map key or Set element. Keys compare lexicographically by first, then rest. Map.keys and Set.toList return ascending key order.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.NonEmptyList
@test
function nonEmptyExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  match NonEmptyList.fromList([3, 4]) with
    case Result.Ok(checked) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: NonEmptyList.head(checked), expected: 3)
      Assert.equal(actual: NonEmptyList.tail(checked), expected: [4])
      bind mapped <- NonEmptyList.map(value: checked, f: lambda(value) return Integer.toString(value) end lambda)
      Assert.equal(actual: NonEmptyList.toList(mapped), expected: ["3", "4"])
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("nonempty input was rejected")
  end match
end function
```

```benitoite
@opaque
public record NonEmptyList[T]
  first: T
  rest: List[T]
end record
```

A first element and a possibly empty tail. Use fromList and the public projections.

```benitoite
public data EmptyListError
  EmptyList
end data
```

Construction failed because the input list was empty. The input list is not retained.

```benitoite
public function fromList[T](values: List[T]) -> Result[NonEmptyList[T], EmptyListError]
```

Checks whether the list is nonempty. Even a constant empty input returns Result.Error.

```benitoite
public function toList[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> List[T]
```

Returns all elements in the original order, preserving shared Reference elements.

```benitoite
public function head[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> T
```

Returns the first element, without a second check or an Option wrapper.

```benitoite
public function tail[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> List[T]
```

Returns the remaining elements, which may be empty.

```benitoite
public function map[T, U, effect E](value: NonEmptyList[T], f: function(value: T) -> U uses E) -> NonEmptyList[U] uses E
```

Applies f once to each element, from first to last. Effects and failures propagate; a successful result remains nonempty.
"}

{"byteLength":6897,"contentHash":{"algorithm":"sha256","value":"1c90717f9021584f160607e2867805c1f441e7a1911e292358b5e665a86c5713"},"kind":"skillDocument","name":"references/stdlib/Range.md","producer":{"build":{"commit":"e6247c11712466a387e46d16147dcc819e6e797a","dirty":null,"provenance":{"commit":"git","dirty":"notCollected"},"target":"aarch64-apple-darwin"},"name":"benitoite","version":"0.0.10"},"schemaVersion":1,"text":"# Benitoite.Range

Status: unofficial. Import it with `import Benitoite.Unofficial.Range`. When the module becomes standard, the import name changes to `import Benitoite.Range`.

Refer to its declarations as `Range.<name>`, for example `Range.CheckedInteger`.

Pure inclusive Integer range checks. Success retains both bounds and the value; bounds may differ between values of the same CheckedInteger type.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Range
@test
function rangeExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  match Range.checkInteger(minimum: 1, maximum: 10, value: 10) with
    case Result.Ok(value) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.minimum(value), expected: 1)
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.maximum(value), expected: 10)
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.value(value), expected: 10)
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("inclusive bound did not match")
  end match
  match Range.checkInteger(minimum: 10, maximum: 1, value: 0) with
    case Result.Error(Range.RangeError.InvalidBounds(low, high)) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: low, expected: 10)
      Assert.equal(actual: high, expected: 1)
    case _ -> Assert.fail("reversed bounds must take priority")
  end match
end function
```

Invalid constant inputs are still Result.Error values, so this checks successfully.

```benitoite check
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Range
function main() -> Unit
  bind result <- Range.checkInteger(minimum: 1, maximum: 10, value: 11)
  return ()
end function
```

```benitoite error
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Range
function main() -> Unit
  bind value <- Range.CheckedInteger(minimum: 1, maximum: 10, value: 5)
  return ()
end function
```
```diagnostic
E0340
```

Checked lengths and indices retain their original immutable list. In particular, get takes only a checked index; a different list must be checked again. Reference elements remain shared.
When the element type supports equality, = compares every stored field structurally, including the original list: minimum/maximum/length/values for CheckedLength and values/index/element for CheckedIndex. Assert failure output shows these internal field names and values; it does not make their automatic accessors public. These wrappers do not implement Trait.Show.
When the element type is a key type, both wrappers are key types and can be Map keys or Set elements. Keys compare lexicographically in stored field declaration order: minimum, maximum, length, values for CheckedLength; values, index, element for CheckedIndex. Map.keys and Set.toList return ascending key order.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Range
@test
function checkedListExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  match Range.checkLength(minimum: 2, maximum: 2, values: [10, 20]) with
    case Result.Ok(value) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.checkedLength(value), expected: 2)
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.lengthValues(value), expected: [10, 20])
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("exact length was rejected")
  end match
  match Range.checkIndex(index: 1, values: [10, 20]) with
    case Result.Ok(value) -> Assert.equal(actual: Range.get(value), expected: 20)
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("valid index was rejected")
  end match
end function
```

```benitoite
@opaque
public record CheckedInteger
  minimum: Integer
  maximum: Integer
  value: Integer
end record
```

An Integer together with the inclusive bounds it satisfies. Use checkInteger and the public projections.

```benitoite
public data RangeError
  InvalidBounds(Integer, Integer)
  OutOfRange(Integer, Integer, Integer)
end data
```

InvalidBounds takes priority over OutOfRange. Failures retain the original inputs.

```benitoite
public function checkInteger(minimum: Integer, maximum: Integer, value: Integer) -> Result[CheckedInteger, RangeError]
```

Checks minimum <= value <= maximum, rejecting reversed bounds first. Constant invalid inputs still return Result.Error. No upper-bound addition is used.

```benitoite
public function minimum(value: CheckedInteger) -> Integer
```

Returns the inclusive lower bound retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function maximum(value: CheckedInteger) -> Integer
```

Returns the inclusive upper bound retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function value(value: CheckedInteger) -> Integer
```

Returns the checked Integer. Call checkInteger again to check it against different bounds.

```benitoite
@opaque
public record CheckedLength[T]
  minimum: Integer
  maximum: Integer
  length: Integer
  values: List[T]
end record
```

A list and its checked inclusive length bounds. This wrapper retains the original list, including references in its elements.

```benitoite
public data LengthError
  InvalidBounds(Integer, Integer)
  OutOfRange(Integer, Integer, Integer)
end data
```

InvalidBounds takes priority over OutOfRange. Failures retain only bounds and the actual length, never the list.

```benitoite
public function checkLength[T](minimum: Integer, maximum: Integer, values: List[T]) -> Result[CheckedLength[T], LengthError]
```

Checks the element count. A negative minimum or reversed bounds is rejected before comparing the length. Constant invalid inputs still return Result.Error.

```benitoite
public function lengthMinimum[T](value: CheckedLength[T]) -> Integer
```

Returns the inclusive minimum length retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function lengthMaximum[T](value: CheckedLength[T]) -> Integer
```

Returns the inclusive maximum length retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function checkedLength[T](value: CheckedLength[T]) -> Integer
```

Returns the element count at the successful check.

```benitoite
public function lengthValues[T](value: CheckedLength[T]) -> List[T]
```

Returns the original immutable list. Its elements, including Reference values, remain shared.

```benitoite
@opaque
public record CheckedIndex[T]
  values: List[T]
  index: Integer
  element: T
end record
```

A list, its checked zero-based index and the element found there. This wrapper retains the original list.

```benitoite
public data IndexError
  OutOfBounds(Integer, Integer)
end data
```

The rejected index and the element count. The original list is not retained.

```benitoite
public function checkIndex[T](index: Integer, values: List[T]) -> Result[CheckedIndex[T], IndexError]
```

Checks the zero-based index and retains its successful element. Both negative and too-large indices return OutOfBounds, including constant inputs.

```benitoite
public function indexValue[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> Integer
```

Returns the zero-based index retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function indexValues[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> List[T]
```

Returns the original immutable list retained by the check.

```benitoite
public function get[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> T
```

Returns the element found during construction. A different list requires a new checkIndex call.

Status: unofficial. Import it with `import Benitoite.Unofficial.Scope`. When the module becomes standard, the import name changes to `import Benitoite.Scope`.

Refer to its declarations as `Scope.<name>`, for example `Scope.CheckedHost`.

Checks host and absolute-path spelling against an explicit scope. Success preserves the condition and target; it does not grant permission or guarantee DNS resolution, filesystem identity, isolation, or IO success.

Use the public checks and projections. These checks do not authorize IO.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Scope
@test
function scopeExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  match Scope.checkHost(pattern: "*.example.com", host: "API.EXAMPLE.COM") with
    case Result.Ok(value) -> Assert.equal(actual: Scope.host(value), expected: "api.example.com")
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("host did not match")
  end match
  match Scope.checkPath(pattern: "/data/**", path: "/data/report.txt") with
    case Result.Ok(value) -> Assert.equal(actual: Scope.path(value), expected: "/data/report.txt")
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("path did not match")
  end match
  match Scope.checkEndpoint(hostPattern: "example.com", host: "example.com", minimumPort: 443, maximumPort: 443, port: 443) with
    case Result.Ok(value) -> Assert.equal(actual: Scope.endpointPort(value), expected: 443)
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("endpoint did not match")
  end match
end function
```

```benitoite error
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Scope
function main() -> Unit
  bind value <- Scope.CheckedHost(pattern: "example.com", host: "example.com")
  return ()
end function
```


```benitoite error
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Scope
function main() -> Unit
  bind result <- Scope.checkHost(pattern: "*.example.com", host: "example.com")
  return ()
end function
```
```diagnostic
E0462
```

```benitoite
  host: String
```


An absolute path and its exact or tree pattern, with spelling preserved.

```benitoite
  maximumPort: Integer

```

A lowercase host and an inclusive port range, retaining all five inputs.

```benitoite

  InvalidTarget(String, String)

  InvalidPort(Integer)

end data
```

Failures retain original inputs. Forms are checked before membership.

Checks an exact host, *.host (one label), or **.host (one or more labels). Wildcards exclude the stem itself. Known invalid direct arguments are rejected before execution.

Status: standard. Import it with `import Benitoite.StringBuilder`.

Function-local string construction. Import Benitoite.StringBuilder explicitly.
Declare with bind b: StringBuilder <- StringBuilder.new(). Local operations add no effects; effects from ordinary arguments are preserved.
A builder is a second-class value: it cannot be stored in an ordinary variable,
returned from a function, or captured by a lambda or lazy expression.
Its kind name is not an ordinary type; builders cannot be ordinary function arguments.
Use copy to obtain an immutable String before capturing or storing a value.
Builders cannot cross lambda, lazy, partial-application, or handler-clause boundaries.
appendAll accepts previously prepared fragments; callbacks cannot capture the builder.


```text
StringBuilder.append(builder: StringBuilder, text: String) -> Unit uses State
```


Pure property trials with explicit random state and bounded shrinking.
Budgets count candidate trials and individual generation/continuation calls.
Callback time and allocation still depend on the input and callback implementation.

```benitoite test
import Benitoite.Unofficial.Test.Property
@test
function propertyExample() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  bind config <- Property.Config(seed: 42, trials: 3, size: 4, maxShrinks: 10, maxShrinkWork: 20)
  bind result <- Property.check(config: config, gen: Property.constant(7), shrinker: Property.shrinkInteger(), property: lambda(value)
    return if value = 7 then Result.Ok(()) else Result.Error("expected seven") end if
  end lambda)
  match result with
    case Result.Ok(_) -> return ()
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("property failed")
  end match
end function
```

```benitoite
end record
```

A pure generator. Direct calls interpret size according to the stored function.

```benitoite
end record
```

Ordered steps; check does not require equality on T.

```benitoite

  Yield(T, function() -> ShrinkStep[T])
  Skip(function() -> ShrinkStep[T])
end data
```

One pure shrinking step. Continuations are called only when the consumer advances.


Maps yielded values, preserving Skip and deferring every continuation.

```benitoite

```

Appends a deferred sequence; reaching left's Done returns a Skip before calling right.

```benitoite
  seed: Integer
  trials: Integer
  size: Integer
  maxShrinks: Integer
  maxShrinkWork: Integer
end record
```

Inclusive budgets: trials 1..10000, size 0..10000, maxShrinks 0..100000, maxShrinkWork 0..1000000.

```benitoite
  original: T
  reduced: T

  message: String

  shrinkWork: Integer

end record
```

A failing input and its replay information. reduced is not necessarily minimal.

```benitoite
end data
```

Configuration errors never call the generator, shrinker, or property.

Returns a value without advancing the generator.

Transforms generated values without inventing an inverse shrinker.

Generates left then right, passing the next random state and the same size.


Inclusive bounds, with deliberate bias to zero and endpoints; not uniform.


Generates false or true from a single 0/1 draw.


Chooses 0, 1, -1, or a finite nextFloat-derived value in [-1, 1).

Generates valid Unicode scalars, including non-ASCII, with length 0..size. Direct run requires size in 0..10000.

Generates 0..size elements, passing the same size to each element generator. Direct run requires size in 0..10000.

Chooses None with probability 1/4, otherwise generating Some.

Tries zero, then successive halves toward zero, without negating the input.

Tries zero and a finite half; zero has no candidates. Non-finite inputs try zero.

The modules of the standard library. Each module has its own file in this directory. Unofficial modules may change; their import name changes when they become standard.

IOError, NetworkError, Json.ParseError, and Csv.ParseError implement Trait.Show by returning their message string unchanged, without added quotes or locations. The first two implementations live in Trait; the ParseError implementations live in Json and Csv. Json.Codec.ConversionError is an extensible conversion failure; its Show displays the relative path and expected/found kinds, without automatically including the input payload or reason. Codec conversions are pure Results. A Result error used with `or die` requires Show; `or return` and bare try do not. Option's die cause is fixed and needs no Show. Explicit Trait.Show.show calls require `import Benitoite.Trait`; die connects its standard references internally without adding names to the user's scope.

Parameter names in these declarations are part of the function contract. Label every argument of an ordinary call with two or more parameters, including calls through function values. Callback names and their order must match the nested function type, even for one parameter. For example, List.map expects `value`, List.fold expects `acc, value`, and Result.mapError expects `error`. An existing function with different names needs an explicit lambda wrapper. See [Idioms](../idioms.md#calls-callback-contracts-holes-and-pipes) for examples.

【決定】初回リリース（`0.0.1`）は、ソースコードだけのリリースとし、実行ファイルを配らない。git のタグは `v0.0.1` とする。以後のソースだけのリリースは `0.0.2`・`0.0.3`…とし、実行ファイルを配る最初のリリースを `0.1.0` とする（版の表は[ロードマップ](../00-overview/00-03-roadmap.md)の「バージョンとコードネーム」）。`0.0.x` のリリースで利用者が処理系を導入する手順は、後述の「ソースからのビルド」だけである。理由: 実行ファイルを配るには、環境ごとのビルドと試験を行うリリースのスクリプトが要り、それを初回リリースの後に回したからである。
【決定】第三者のライセンスの表示 `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES` は、次のように作り、示す。
- `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES` は、開発機の上で cargo-about を使って生成する（`scripts/release/licenses.sh`）。依存のクレートはビルド先によって違いうるので、ビルド先ごとに生成する。
- 【方針】`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES` には、実行ファイルに含む依存のクレートごとに、名前・版・ライセンス・著作権表示・ライセンス文を載せ、Apache-2.0 のものは NOTICE ファイルの内容も載せる（[ロードマップ](../00-overview/00-03-roadmap.md)の「利用する既存の OSS のライセンス」）。

- 【決定】配布物（crates.io のパッケージ）のライセンスの文に著作権の行がないクレートは、そのクレートの `Cargo.toml` の `authors` を著作者として添える。ライセンスのファイルがパッケージにないクレートは、そのライセンスの SPDX の標準の文を載せ、`authors` を添える。上流のリポジトリの文を取って補うことはせず、`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES` はネットワークを使わずに、ロックファイルと取得済みのパッケージだけから生成できるようにする。理由: 生成の結果が、ネットワークの状態や上流のリポジトリの変化に左右されないようにするためである。

- 機能 `bundled-licenses` を付けたビルドは、生成した `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES` を処理系のクレートの `licenses/` に置いたうえで、実行ファイルに埋め込む。`benitoite --licenses` は、埋め込んだ一覧を標準出力に書く（[CLI](../06-tooling/06-01-cli.md)の「コマンドラインの形」）。生成したファイルはリポジトリで追跡しない。生成と埋め込みをまとめて行うリリースのスクリプトは初回リリース版に含めない（docs/todo の TODO-073）。

@test("checked lists retain their values")
function checkedLists() -> Unit uses Assert.Check
  match Range.checkLength(minimum: 2, maximum: 2, values: [10, 20]) with
    case Result.Ok(checked) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.checkedLength(checked), expected: 2)
      Assert.equal(actual: Range.lengthValues(checked), expected: [10, 20])
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("valid length was rejected")
  end match
  match Range.checkIndex(index: 1, values: [10, 20]) with
    case Result.Ok(checked) -> Assert.equal(actual: Range.get(checked), expected: 20)
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("valid index was rejected")
  end match
  match NonEmptyList.fromList([10, 20]) with
    case Result.Ok(checked) ->
      Assert.equal(actual: NonEmptyList.head(checked), expected: 10)
      Assert.equal(actual: NonEmptyList.tail(checked), expected: [20])
    case Result.Error(_) -> Assert.fail("nonempty list was rejected")
  end match
end function

public record Node[T]
  value: T
